argument:
Frontken's semiconductor-service demand supports a quality-growth purchase scenario: H1 revenue grew 30% and attributable profit 40%. No bank borrowings, RM560.618m cash/deposits and RM961.350m short investments provide capacity for the observed Taiwan expansion. H1 FCF of RM35.491m confirms some realised cash after capex; constructive technicals on above-average volume corroborate current investor interest.

The liquidity increase was partly warrant-funded, with RM636.783m exercise proceeds, and cannot be mistaken for operating cash creation. Receivables absorbed RM80.148m and other income helped profits. At 47.18x trailing and estimated 38.23x forward earnings, continued growth must offset dilution and collection delays. Positive FCF and bank-debt-free financing make expansion feasible, but attractive per-share returns depend on durable service growth and cash conversion. The upper-band close favors patience rather than an automatic breakout entry.
key_points: Service growth, positive FCF and bank-debt-free financing support expansion.
Warrant funding and other income qualify liquidity and profit growth.
Premium valuation requires sustained per-share growth and collection discipline.
